title: Prostate Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Planning

evidenceAudit.scope: Men with suspected or confirmed prostate cancer: referral thresholds, MRI-first diagnosis, risk grouping, choosing active surveillance or radical treatment, hormone therapy and its adverse effects, and metastatic disease. Verified against the Saudi Oncology Society / Saudi Urology Association guideline (2017), NICE NG131 and NICE NG12; doses from NICE and FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi screening policy for asymptomatic men not in PHA 2023
LHRH agonist and newer agent doses not reproduced

pathophysiology.summary: Prostate adenocarcinoma is androgen-driven. Many low-grade cancers grow slowly and never cause harm; high-grade cancers spread to nodes and bone. Grade (Gleason), PSA and stage define risk and treatment. In Saudi Arabia, fewer than half of cases (46.9%) are localised at diagnosis (SOS/SUA).
keyMechanisms: Androgen receptor signalling drives growth — hence androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).
Castration resistance develops over time with continued androgen receptor activity.
Bone metastases are typically sclerotic; ADT itself causes bone loss.

symptoms: Lower urinary tract symptoms, erectile dysfunction, visible haematuria (NICE NG12 1.6.2).
Bone pain, weight loss in advanced disease.
physicalSigns: Digital rectal examination: hard, irregular prostate.
redFlags: Prostate feels malignant on DRE — suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12 1.6.1)
Back pain with leg weakness — suspected spinal cord compression, emergency

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Smooth enlarged gland; PSA may be raised.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Men with LUTS, ED or haematuria after counselling (NICE NG12 1.6.2)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: 40–49: above 2.5; 50–59: above 3.5; 60–69: above 4.5; 70–79: above 6.5 µg/L → consider suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12 Table 2).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Do not biopsy on PSA alone (NICE NG131 1.2.6).
ruleIn.normalValue: At or below age-specific threshold (e.g. 3.5 µg/L or less at 50–59)

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and refer
actions: Counsel, then PSA and DRE for LUTS, ED or visible haematuria (NICE NG12 1.6.2).
Refer if DRE malignant or PSA above age threshold (NICE 1.6.1, 1.6.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose and stratify
actions: MRI first; biopsy if Likert 3 or more (NICE 1.2.2–1.2.3).
Assign Cambridge Prognostic Group 1–5 at MDT (NICE 1.2.15).

clinicalManagement.title: Localised disease
actions: CPG 1: offer active surveillance (NICE 1.3.8). SOS criteria: PSA below 10, Gleason 6 or less, 2 or fewer positive cores, under 50% of any core, PSA density below 0.15.
CPG 2: active surveillance, prostatectomy or radiotherapy (NICE 1.3.9).
CPG 3: radical treatment; surveillance only if the person declines (NICE 1.3.10).
CPG 4–5: no active surveillance; radical treatment if long-term control is likely (NICE 1.3.11–1.3.12).
Radiotherapy for CPG 2–5: add 6 months ADT; consider up to 3 years for CPG 4–5 (NICE 1.3.21–1.3.23).

clinicalManagement.title: Hormone therapy
actions: LHRH agonist with anti-androgen cover for the first 4 weeks to block the flare (SOS/SUA, ADT section).
Bone health: vitamin D and calcium for all on ADT; denosumab or bisphosphonate if T-score below −1.5 (SOS/SUA item 7, bone health); bisphosphonate if osteoporosis (NICE 1.4.14).
Hot flushes: medroxyprogesterone 20 mg daily for 10 weeks (NICE 1.4.3).
Supervised exercise twice weekly for 12 weeks for fatigue (NICE 1.4.19).

clinicalManagement.title: Metastatic disease
actions: Newly diagnosed metastatic, fit: docetaxel 75 mg/m² 3-weekly for 6 cycles, starting within 12 weeks of ADT (NICE 1.5.6); SOS/SUA: six cycles with ADT as standard.
Orchidectomy is an alternative to LHRH agonist (NICE 1.5.7).
Castration-resistant disease: MDT; options include docetaxel, abiraterone, enzalutamide, radium-223 (SOS/SUA).

learningObjectives: Diagnose, risk-stratify and plan treatment for prostate cancer.

keyPoints: ADT: anti-androgen cover for the flare; protect bone.
Docetaxel for fit men with new metastatic disease.
pitfalls: Biopsy on PSA alone without counselling.
Starting LHRH agonist without anti-androgen cover in high-volume disease.

patientEducation: Explain surveillance vs treatment trade-offs, sexual and urinary effects, and ADT side effects.
lifestyleAndDiet: Supervised resistance and aerobic exercise on ADT (NICE 1.4.19).
mdtReferrals: Urology MDT; oncology; erectile dysfunction service (NICE 1.4.8).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: After curative therapy: PSA at 3, 6 and 12 months, every 6 months for 3 years, then yearly (SOS). Active surveillance: PSA every 3–4 months in year 1, MRI at 12–18 months, then PSA 6-monthly (NICE Table 2).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: One of: Gleason 8, PSA above 20, T3
Two or more of these, or Gleason 9–10, or T4

regimens.indication: Newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer, no significant comorbidity
regimens.duration: 6 cycles, starting within 12 weeks of ADT
adjustments: Premedicate with dexamethasone 8 mg orally at 12, 3 and 1 hour before infusion (label, prostate regimen)
Avoid if bilirubin above ULN or transaminases above 1.5 × ULN with ALP above 2.5 × ULN (label)
monitoring: Bilirubin, AST/ALT, ALP before each cycle
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG131: Prostate cancer: diagnosis and management
contraindications: Severe hypersensitivity to docetaxel or polysorbate 80
Avoid if bilirubin above ULN, or AST/ALT above 1.5 × ULN with ALP above 2.5 × ULN (boxed warning)

regimens.indication: Troublesome hot flushes on long-term ADT
adjustments: If ineffective, cyproterone 50 mg twice daily for 4 weeks may be considered (NICE 1.4.4)
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG131: Prostate cancer: diagnosis and management
contraindications: Active or past arterial thromboembolic disease (stroke, MI)
Known or suspected oestrogen- or progesterone-dependent neoplasia; breast cancer
Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; pregnancy (labelled for women)

regimens.indication: Metastatic disease, person wishes to preserve sexual function
regimens.patientGroup: Men accepting reduced survival and gynaecomastia
regimens.duration: Until sexual function not maintained — then switch to ADT (NICE 1.5.10)
adjustments: 150 mg monotherapy is not FDA-approved; off-label in UK (NICE note)
Breast-bud radiotherapy within first month if over 6 months' use (NICE 1.4.16)
monitoring: Transaminases before starting, regularly for 4 months, then periodically (label)
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG131: Prostate cancer: diagnosis and management

regimens.indication: Bone loss on ADT at high fracture risk (T-score below −1.5 per SOS)
regimens.duration: While on ADT and at risk
adjustments: Correct hypocalcaemia first; calcium and vitamin D supplements (label; SOS: calcium 1,200 mg and vitamin D 800 IU daily)
Check for CKD-mineral bone disorder in advanced CKD before starting (label)

medicationPlan.note: Docetaxel, medroxyprogesterone and bicalutamide doses from NICE NG131 (checked against FDA labels); denosumab dose from the FDA label with the SOS bone-health threshold. LHRH agonist/antagonist and androgen receptor pathway inhibitor doses are product- and protocol-specific — not reproduced. Check SFDA registration.

values: Active surveillance; radical options if life expectancy over 10 years
Intermediate 6 months; high risk 18 months–3 years
